title: Default run stays review-only, BUT a fix:true path (effort:low) ran 2026-06-21T03:52 and applied 5 fixes — review-only is the common but NOT universal default
detail: Most orchestrator runs stay review-only (review.fix.mode='review-only'). EXCEPTIONS: 2026-06-20T04:11 (effort:medium+fix:true, 2 fixes, 0 regressions, tests 546->546); and 2026-06-21T03:52 (effort:low+fix:true, 5 fixes applied, 0 regressions) — the FIRST effort:low+fix:true run in this history to apply non-zero fixes, and the largest single-run applied-fix count so far (5 > prior high of 2). The ux lane auto-applies its own 3 fixes via its own dryRun:false path, independent of review fix.mode. The review fix path is now VERIFIED WORKING at BOTH effort tiers (medium AND low), on clean trees. 2026-06-20T19:03, 2026-06-20T19:44, 2026-06-20T23:11, 2026-06-21T02:18 (effort:low defaults) were review-only (fix.mode='review-only'). 2026-06-21T03:52 (effort:low+fix:true) was the first low-tier non-review-only run. The review-only default holds when fix:true is NOT passed; passing fix:true overrides it at both tiers.

title: openIssues trend is wildly non-monotone: 11->14->12->1->0->21->172->174->22->19->10->1->26->0->0->2->1->1->2->33 across runs; code churn refills the queue
detail: openIssues went 11,14,12,1,0,21,172,174,22,19,10,1,26,0,0,2,1,1,2,33 (2026-06-21T03:52 review+schema+lint run, verified=33 from newFindings=48, high=2, medium=12, low=19, rejection_rate (48-33)/48~0.3125). The 0->21->172->174 escalation after the 06-16 clean run confirmed the baseline was fragile and code churn refills the queue aggressively. The 22->19->10->1 decline on 2026-06-19/2020-03:22 reflected shrinking changed-file surface PLUS post-W4 verify filtering. 2026-06-20T04:11 JUMPED to 26 (verified=26, adversarial 2/2 upheld) — an effort:medium FULL-scope scan (191 files), not incremental. 2026-06-20T06:07 AND 2026-06-20T11:19 returned openIssues=0 on small incremental scopes (the latter verified=0 from newFindings=3, all 3 rejected by the gate). 2026-06-20T13:08 also returned openIssues=0 — but that run omitted the review lane (lanes:['schema','ux']), so openIssues=0 simply means review didn't run, NOT that the code is clean. 2026-06-20T19:03 returned openIssues=2 (verified=2). 2026-06-20T19:44 returned openIssues=1 (verified=1 of newFindings=4, medium=1). 2026-06-20T23:11 returned openIssues=1 (verified=1 of newFindings=7, high=1). 2026-06-21T02:18 returned openIssues=2 (verified=2 of newFindings=3, high=2 — both the caption reader/writer asymmetry bug). 2026-06-21T03:52 returned openIssues=33 (verified=33 of newFindings=48, high=2/medium=12/low=19) — the LARGEST incremental-scope verified count in this history, and a full-scope clean-tree fix:true run that APPLIED 5 of them (so the queue did NOT stay at 33; openIssues is the verified-snapshot, fix.applied clears findings out-of-band). Treat a 0 as 'queue drained' (or review-absent), never 'nothing to find'. NOTE: post-W4 the openIssues count reflects verified (post-filter), so it can be lower than raw newFindings. IMPORTANT: openIssues magnitude is only comparable across runs at the SAME scan scope (incremental vs full) AND only when the review lane actually ran; and on a fix:true run, openIssues is the pre-fix verified count, not the post-fix remainder.

title: schema runtime lane reports ~5 findings on dirty runs, null once, ELEVEN+ consecutive fully-clean 0s when requested
detail: Runtime lane reported ~5 findings on non-clean runs (first run had 8 + 2 errors). On 2026-06-18T13:32 it returned null; on 2026-06-18T15:22, 2026-06-19T18:35, 2026-06-19T21:01, AND 2026-06-19T21:56 it returned runtimeFindings=0, runtimeErrors=0, driftRemaining=0 — fully-clean schema lane results. 2026-06-20T13:08 (lanes:['schema','ux']) and 2026-06-20T19:03 (lanes:[review,schema]) both returned schema={runtimeFindings:0, runtimeErrors:0, driftRemaining:0, coverageDelta:'n/a'} NON-null. 2026-06-20T19:44, 2026-06-20T23:11, 2026-06-21T02:18, AND 2026-06-21T03:52 (lanes:[review,schema,lint]) again schema={0,0,0,n/a} — the clean-streak now spans 11+ consecutive runs. The runtime lane (buildCliArgs->run.py boundary) is productive on churn but goes quiet when the tree is clean; a 0 is now firmly interpretable as clean (distinct from the null failure mode). Check schemaHistory path when schema=null AND 'schema' was in the requested lanes.

title: runtimeErrors only appeared in the first run (2); zero across all runs since
detail: First run had 2 runtimeErrors + 8 runtimeFindings; all subsequent runs (now 15 total, incl 2026-06-21T03:52 runtimeErrors=0) have 0 errors. Either the boundary stabilized or earlier runs' findings were resolved out-of-band. Don't assume errors are gone — re-run objective:runtime after any CLI change.

title: coverageDelta is NaN/n/a on every run — coverage lane never runs under objective:runtime
detail: All runs set objective:runtime (default), so coverageDelta reports 'NaN' or 'n/a' every time (now 15 runs confirmed, incl 2026-06-21T03:52 schema coverageDelta='n/a'). To get a real coverage trend you must pass objective:coverage|both|all; the default lane produces no coverage signal.

title: driftRemaining is 0 on all runs — GUI<->run.py flags stay aligned
detail: driftRemaining=0 across all runs (now 15 with signal, incl 2026-06-21T03:52 review+schema+lint run). Either drift is genuinely clean or check:schema was already applied earlier. Drift lane is currently a low-value no-op; budget agent time on the runtime lane instead.

title: Verified review findings severity is run-dependent; medium dominates incremental high-volume runs, low dominates full-scope scans, critical is volume-orthogonal, a tiny incremental scan's survivors can be ALL HIGH, AND a high-volume run's verified mix tracks the raw mix
detail: Severity distribution varies per run. 2026-06-18T13:32: high=5, medium=12, low=4. 2026-06-18T15:22: high=6, medium=13, low=2. 2026-06-19T18:35: high=2, medium=3, low=4 (lowest total=9, low-dominant). 2026-06-19T21:01: high=3, medium=15, low=4 (total=22, MEDIUM-dominant). 2026-06-19T21:56: critical=1, high=4, medium=8, low=6 (total=19). 2026-06-19T22:46: critical=1, high=1, medium=4, low=4 (total=10, low TIES medium). 2026-06-20T03:22: medium=1 (total VERIFIED=1). 2026-06-20T04:11 (effort:medium FULL scope): high=2, medium=6, low=16, info=2 (total VERIFIED=26) — the first run with an `info` bucket, LOW dominates because a full-scope scan surfaces many low-severity style/quality nits. 2026-06-20T06:07: VERIFIED=0. 2026-06-20T11:19: newFindings=3 but VERIFIED=0 (bySeverity map EMPTY). 2026-06-20T13:08: review lane NOT requested. 2026-06-20T19:03: VERIFIED=2, bySeverity={low:2}. 2026-06-20T19:44: VERIFIED=1, bySeverity={medium:1}. 2026-06-20T23:11: VERIFIED=1, bySeverity={high:1}. 2026-06-21T02:18 (effort:low, FULL-scope 156 files): VERIFIED=2, bySeverity={high:2} — FIRST run where ALL survivors were HIGH and the two findings shared ONE root cause (caption reader/writer asymmetry, lib/knowledge-extractor.ts). 2026-06-21T03:52 (effort:low+fix:true, FULL-scope via clean-tree): VERIFIED=33, bySeverity={high:2, medium:12, low=19} (newFindings=48, ~0.31 rejection) — the LARGEST verified count in this history, and the verified mix roughly tracks the raw mix (low-dominant at volume, exactly like the full-scope 04:11 run). Pattern sharpens: medium is the modal bucket on incremental high-volume runs (>=12); on a FULL-scope run LOW dominates (style nits); high stays in a narrow 1-6 band on volume runs but can be the SOLE or ENTIRE survivor set of a small-scope scan (23:11 single-high, 02:18 double-high-same-root-cause); critical is rare (2 in 20 runs) but when it appears it is the highest-priority fix target; a rejection_rate=1.0 run always yields an EMPTY bySeverity map; a small verified-count run can be low-only (19:03), medium-only (19:44), OR high-only (23:11).

title: review-only runs report findings but don't fix them; openIssues=0 can also mean the review lane didn't run; fix:true runs DO clear (5 applied 2026-06-21T03:52)
detail: Most runs have review.fix.mode='review-only' (fix:false). The 11->1->0 openIssues drop between 06-15 and 06-16 happened WITHOUT any review fix:true run — the backlog was cleared outside the orchestrator. The 0->21->172->174 escalation confirmed the queue refills as code changes. EXCEPTION 2026-06-20T04:11: effort:medium+fix:true applied 2 fixes (0 regressions). EXCEPTION 2026-06-21T03:52: effort:low+fix:true applied 5 fixes (0 regressions) — the FIRST low-tier fix:true run to apply non-zero fixes, and the largest applied count so far. NOTE: on a fix:true run openIssues (33 here) is the PRE-fix verified snapshot; fix.applied=5 clears those out-of-band, so the post-fix remainder is lower. 2026-06-20T13:08 (lanes:['schema','ux'], review NOT requested) returned openIssues=0 because the review lane didn't run — a review-absent run ALWAYS yields openIssues=0 regardless of code state; this is NOT a clean signal. 2026-06-20T19:03 (review-only) openIssues=2. 2026-06-20T19:44 (review-only) openIssues=1. 2026-06-20T23:11 (review-only) openIssues=1 (high=1 — a HIGH-severity finding remained queued because review-only does not fix). 2026-06-21T02:18 (review-only) openIssues=2 (high=2, caption asymmetry). A clean review-only run is not evidence the code is clean, only that nothing new was verified OR that review didn't run. Before treating openIssues=0 as 'queue drained', confirm 'review' was in the requested lanes.

title: delta_from_last is null on every run — inter-run delta tracking is not wired
detail: signals.delta_from_last is null in all runs (2026-06-21T03:52 confirms again), so you cannot read 'better/worse than last run' from the envelope. Compute deltas yourself from openIssues/verified/runtimeFindings across history files — but only compare runs at the SAME scan scope (incremental vs full) and only when the same lanes ran.

title: Orchestrator completes with empty phases_failed on every run
detail: status='complete' and phases_failed=[] on all runs, even ones that surfaced runtimeErrors, 174 openIssues, or a null schema lane. 2026-06-20T19:03 again phases_failed=[] despite 2 open review findings. 2026-06-20T19:44 (3-lane review+schema+lint) again phases_failed=[] despite 1 open review finding. 2026-06-20T23:11 (3-lane) again phases_failed=[] despite 1 open HIGH finding. 2026-06-21T02:18 (3-lane) again phases_failed=[] despite 2 open HIGH findings. 2026-06-21T03:52 (3-lane, fix:true) again phases_failed=[] despite 33 open review findings (5 of which were applied as fixes). Don't treat 'complete' as 'no problems' — phase success only means the lane ran, not that the code is healthy. Read result.review/schema/ux/lint for actual signal.

title: dirtyTree was false on all runs INCLUDING both fix:true runs — the dirty-tree downgrade never fired (every fix:true opportunity landed on a clean tree)
detail: dirtyTree was false in all runs. 2026-06-20T04:11 (effort:medium+fix:true, treeDirty=false) and 2026-06-21T03:52 (effort:low+fix:true, clean tree) BOTH proceeded and applied fixes (2 then 5, 0 regressions each). This means the 'fix:true gets downgraded to review-only on a dirty git tree' guard still has NOT actually fired here (every fix:true opportunity landed on a clean tree). The guard's downgrade behavior remains unverified — test it deliberately (stage uncommitted WIP, then invoke fix:true) before trusting it rejects the fix. The intervening runs were review-only (no fix path exercised).

title: SUPERSEDED: verified != newFindings once the W4 consolidated verify gate runs — see gotcha-verified-neq-newfindings
detail: Originally recorded (2026-06-14..2026-06-19) that result.review.verified always equals result.review.newFindings (no verify filtering). SUPERSEDED by 2026-06-20T03:22: that run had newFindings=4 but verified=1 — the W4 consolidated adversarial-verify gate (EFFORT_CONFIG.low.adversarial changed from 'skip' to fail-open-filter) now rejects findings, so verified can be strictly LESS than newFindings. The equality held only because the pre-W4 gate was skipped. This record is kept for trend continuity; read gotcha-verified-neq-newfindings for current behavior.

title: schema lane can silently return null — but also returns full data when healthy (intermittent)
detail: On 2026-06-18T13:32 the schema result field was null despite schema being in lanes. The 2026-06-18T15:22, 2026-06-19T18:35, 2026-06-19T21:01, and 2026-06-19T21:56 runs show the lane CAN return full data (runtimeFindings=0, driftRemaining=0) — so null is a genuine intermittent failure mode, not a constant. The schemaHistory path (gui-movie-director-schema-self-improve/iterations.jsonl) is the authoritative log; null result may mean internal error. Always check schemaHistory when schema=null. NOTE: on 2026-06-19T22:46, 2026-06-20T03:22, 2026-06-20T04:11, 2026-06-20T06:07, AND 2026-06-20T11:19 the runs used lanes:[review] ONLY (no schema lane requested), so schema=null is EXPECTED. 2026-06-20T13:08, 2026-06-20T19:03, 2026-06-20T19:44, 2026-06-20T23:11, 2026-06-21T02:18, AND 2026-06-21T03:52 returned schema NON-null (0/0/0), confirming 'schema requested' does reliably return data when healthy.

title: No stable baseline: clean runs are immediately re-broken by code churn; full-scope scans reset the count
detail: The 2026-06-16 clean run (openIssues=0) was broken within hours — 21, 172, 174, then 22, 19, 10, 1 (incremental, post-W4). 2026-06-20T04:11 was effort:medium FULL-scope (191 files) and reported openIssues=26 — a different MAGNITUDE because it is a full-surface count, not incremental. No clean baseline has survived to the next run. Re-establishing a baseline requires a fix:true run to clear the queue AND a code-churn freeze; review-only runs cannot produce a durable baseline. Compare only runs at the SAME scan scope when trending.

title: SUPERSEDED: the 21-finding spike was dwarfed by a 172-finding run hours later
detail: Recorded the 2026-06-18T13:32 21-finding spike as the largest single-run count. SUPERSEDED by openissues-172-spike-three-lane which shows the same code-churn driver producing 172 findings (8x larger) just hours later, and the non-monotone pattern (openissues-converges-to-zero) is the durable insight. This specific spike magnitude is no longer the high-water mark.

title: 174 openIssues high-water mark was a 3-lane ux-contaminated run; post-uxAuto-fix pure-code runs sit ~1-33 (scope-dependent)
detail: The 2026-06-19T18:35 run produced 174 openIssues = review.newFindings(9) + ux.totalIssues(165), ~95% ux-sourced. That was the high-water mark UNDER the old openIssues formula (review+schema+drift+ux). After the uxAuto gate fix (2026-06-19T18:51), the pure review-only/review+schema runs produced openIssues=22, 19, 10, 1 (incremental) — and 2026-06-20T04:11 (effort:medium FULL-scope) produced 26 (verified=26). 2026-06-20T19:03 (incremental) produced openIssues=2. 2026-06-20T19:44 produced openIssues=1. 2026-06-20T23:11 produced openIssues=1. 2026-06-21T02:18 (FULL-scope 156 files) produced openIssues=2. 2026-06-21T03:52 (effort:low+fix:true, FULL-scope clean tree) produced openIssues=33 (verified=33, high=2/medium=12/low=19) — the largest PURE-CODE verified count post-uxAuto-fix (no ux contamination), and a fix:true run that APPLIED 5 of them. When ux lane is enabled, openIssues is NOT comparable to review-only figures — always split result.ux.totalIssues from result.review.newFindings before trending. Also: never trend a full-scope count against an incremental count.

title: RETIRED: ux totalIssues (165) used to dwarf review newFindings (9) — openIssues formula fixed to exclude ux (see lever-openissues-code-only)
detail: Second ux-lane run: ux.totalIssues=165 vs review.newFindings=9; merged openIssues=174 was ~95% ux-sourced (up from 88% on the first ux run). Retired because the openIssues formula was fixed (2026-06-19) to EXCLUDE ux (openIssues = review verified + schema runtimeErrors + remaining drift); the durable 'ux excluded, tracked separately' insight is captured in lever-openissues-code-only (confirmed stable across 14 runs incl 2026-06-21T03:52). Only historical value remains.

title: ux auto-fix lifts avg score ~0.5 points per run fixing only 3 of ~150 issues
detail: The 2026-06-18T15:22 ux lane surveyed 23 views (avg 4.82/10) and auto-fixed 3 issues, raising the average to 5.36/10 (+0.54). The 2026-06-19T18:35 run surveyed 23 views (avg 3.91/10) and auto-fixed 3 issues, raising to 4.43/10 (+0.52). The ux fix path is functional and applies fixes via its own dryRun:false control — independent of review.fix.mode (which stayed review-only). The +0.5/3-fix lever ratio is consistent across two runs. Note: avg DROPPED 5.36->3.91 between runs (different view mix / churn re-introduced regressions), so absolute score is not yet monotone — but the per-run fix delta is stable. CAVEAT (2026-06-20T13:08): a third ux run applied ZERO fixes (issuesFixed=0, score flat 4.96->4.96) — the fix path is conditional (dryRun or no auto-fixable candidate); see ux-baseline-low-score-ceiling. (The review lane's fix path is ALSO now verified working at BOTH effort tiers — see lever-medium-fix-applies-real-fixes, updated for the 2026-06-21T03:52 low-tier 5-fix run.)

title: UX avg score baseline hovers ~4-5/10 across 23 views; absolute score is non-monotone AND the fix-count can be 0
detail: Three ux-lane baselines now: 2026-06-18T15:22 avgScoreBefore=4.82, 2026-06-19T18:35 avgScoreBefore=3.91 (DOWN 0.91 despite a +0.52 fix delta the prior run), 2026-06-20T13:08 avgScoreBefore=4.96 (issuesFixed=0, avgScoreAfter=4.96 — score FLAT). The before-score dropped/rebounded between runs because code churn re-introduced UX regressions between runs. Even after fixing 3 each time, avg only reaches ~4.4-5.4/10. NEW: the 2026-06-20T13:08 run surveyed 23 views (127 issues) but applied ZERO fixes (issuesFixed=0) and the score was unchanged — so the ux lane CAN run without fixing anything (likely dryRun, or no auto-fixable candidate found). The UX surface has significant debt (field clarity, loading states, empty states) that the review/schema lanes cannot surface, AND fixes do not durably stick — the same views re-regress. The ux lane is the only lane that sees this surface; it is additive signal, but a single fix run is not durable without a code-churn freeze. A flat-score (issuesFixed=0) run is NOT a regression — it is a no-fix survey.

title: schema lane returned a fully-clean result (0 findings, 0 errors, 0 drift) — now ELEVEN+ consecutive clean runs incl review+schema+lint runs
detail: 2026-06-18T15:22 was the first schema lane result with runtimeFindings=0, runtimeErrors=0, AND driftRemaining=0 simultaneously; 2026-06-19T18:35, 2026-06-19T21:01, and 2026-06-19T21:56 repeat it. 2026-06-20T13:08, 2026-06-20T19:03, 2026-06-20T19:44, 2026-06-20T23:11, 2026-06-21T02:18, AND 2026-06-21T03:52 repeat it again: schema={runtimeFindings:0, runtimeErrors:0, driftRemaining:0, coverageDelta:'n/a'}. Eleven+ consecutive clean runs suggest the schema->CLI boundary (buildCliArgs->run.py) is currently healthy — the GUI schemas and run.py flags are aligned. Re-confirm after any CLI/schema edit; a 0 is now interpretable as genuinely clean (distinct from the null failure mode).

title: Command views render a blank/black main panel with no form on first navigation
detail: The dominant UX defect class: several views (t2i, video-quality, video-generate, faceswap, model-check, jobs) render an empty black void on first load because CommandForm only mounts AFTER useDefaultState resolves server defaults, and the canvas is bare in the meantime. There is no header, breadcrumb, empty-state, or loading skeleton — the user cannot tell a loading failure from an empty state from a broken render. Affects every createCommandView() view until guarded. The VLM caption reads these as 'a large, empty black panel' / 'no primary action button visible'.

title: Guard CommandViewShell with an actionable empty-state instead of a dead black panel
detail: Adopted fix for blank-panel views: when a view yields no form children (silent render failure), CommandViewShell now renders an actionable 'This view has nothing to show' message plus a .empty-view-state CSS class, so the canvas is never a bare void. Applied to video-quality-01 (score held 2->2 but the panel is no longer dead). Generalizes to every createCommandView view — always provide a non-blocking empty/loading placeholder while useDefaultState resolves or when children fail to mount.

title: Wrap command views in a persistent title header (reuse ModelCheckView inline-style convention)
detail: Adopted fix for blank/unlabeled panels: wrap the generated view (e.g. T2lView) in a container that renders a persistent h2 title plus a dim description line, matching the existing ModelCheckView inline-style convention and reusing --text-bright/--text-dim CSS variables. Result: the main panel is never blank/unlabeled and the user can always tell which view is active. Applied to t2i-01 (score 3->9). This is the higher-impact sibling of the empty-state guard — it also labels healthy renders.

title: Sidebar active-state logic is correct; the CSS is too faint for the VLM (and users) to read as selected
detail: Layout.tsx already computes an `active` class on the sidebar item when currentView.action===cmd.id, so the routing logic is NOT the bug. The defect is that .sidebar-item.active (global.css:91) uses only a faint background + accent left border + accent text that reads as indistinguishable from inactive. Strengthen with an --accent color-mix tinted background + font-weight 600 (adopted in video-quality-02, score 2->8) so the selected item is unmistakable. Do NOT re-investigate the Layout logic when the active cue looks missing.

title: toSections silently discards any schema field without a `section` property
detail: Latent trap: schemas/toForm.ts toSections does `if (!f.section) continue;`, so any field lacking a `section` is silently dropped from the rendered form with NO error. Confirmed instance: faceswap schema's 'LoRA Path' field {key:'lora'} has no section, so the documented LoRA control never appears in the UI and users cannot set a custom face-swap LoRA despite the schema declaring it. Either assign every schema field a section, or make toSections fall back to a default 'Advanced' section instead of dropping sectionless fields.

title: ViewDescriptor id MUST equal the useCommandJob/SCHEMA_MAP action key
detail: Latent routing/state bug: VideoGenerateView registers with descriptor id 'vid-generate', but every other reference uses 'video-generate' (useCommandJob('video-generate'), action='video-generate', SCHEMA_MAP['video-generate']). If routing or useDefaultState keys off the descriptor id, the schema-defaults fetch and action routing resolve against different keys — contributing to blank render and breaking per-view state persistence. Convention: keep the descriptor id identical to the schema action key AND the CLI action, as the sibling video views (VideoRelay etc.) already do.

title: Disabled submit buttons give no reason — no inline hint listing missing required inputs
detail: Recurring UX gap: schema.isDisabled(state) returns true when required inputs are unset (e.g. faceswap input_image/face), greying out the primary action, but nothing in the UI explains WHY or what the user must do. No required-field callout, no helper text, no 'Upload X and Y to enable Z'. A first-time user staring at a disabled button has no path forward. When schema.isDisabled(state) is true, render an InlineError or small hint near the btn-row listing the missing required inputs.

title: Sidebar nav items are non-semantic divs — not keyboard-focusable, no aria-current
detail: Accessibility defect: all navigation entries (Gallery, Config, Jobs, every command) are plain <div> elements with onClick handlers (Layout.tsx). No role='button', no tabIndex, no aria-current — invisible to Tab-key navigation and screen readers cannot announce them. The sidebar <aside> is also not a <nav aria-label>. Fix: render nav items as <button> (or role='button' tabIndex={0} + onKeyDown Enter/Space), wrap in <nav aria-label='Views'>, set aria-current='page' on the active item. A keyboard-only or assistive-tech user cannot reach any view currently.

title: Avg UX score ~4-5/10; ~3 fixes per run (but can be 0), ~17 high-severity issues remain — needs ~8 iters to reach ~7.0
detail: Measured baseline from the 23-view scan: avg UX score 4.82 (first run) / 3.91 (second run) / 4.96 (third run 2026-06-20T13:08, issuesFixed=0), ~127-165 issues total (~20 high). With maxIters:3 and dryRun:false, only 3 fixes applied per run (score ceiling ~4.4-5.4/10), leaving ~17 high-severity issues unfixed. The blank-panel/active-nav/header fixes each move a single view 3-7 points, so the lever-per-iter ratio is high but the volume of low-scoring views (t2i=3, video-quality=2, video-generate=3, faceswap=3, image-restore=4, model-check=4) exceeds a 3-iter budget. Suggested next run: maxIters:8, dryRun:false -> expect avg ~7.0. image-pipeline scored null/0 issues (healthy / not reached) and can be skipped to save budget. NOTE 2026-06-20T13:08: issuesFixed=0 means a ux run can apply NO fixes — confirm dryRun setting before concluding the budget math.

title: VLM caption can misread a correctly-wired feature as missing when the visual cue is too subtle
detail: Recurring false-positive class: the VLM (and by extension users) reports 'No active/selected highlight' and 'no primary action button visible' even when the underlying TS logic is correct. video-quality-02 and t2i-02 both reported a missing active-nav cue, but Layout.tsx already applies the `active` class — the CSS was just too faint. Treat 'feature is missing' captions as visual-prominence problems first (strengthen the CSS) before investigating the logic. Distinguish 'logic absent' from 'logic present but invisible' by reading the source, not by trusting the caption.

title: Absolute-path-as-info-disclosure is a FALSE POSITIVE when the path is functional identity
detail: Review lane flags api/models.ts handleListLoras/handleListVaes returning absolute filesystem paths to the client as 'info disclosure'. But lora.path is LOAD-BEARING: LoraField.tsx uses it as the <option value>, copy-to-clipboard (for CLI reuse), and the selected value flows to run.py --lora. Stripping to basename BREAKS the selector + copy feature. Verified 2026-06-19: grep frontend shows lora.path used as identity key at LoraField.tsx:165/199/204. Suppress this finding class; the threat model is weak anyway (unauthenticated localhost dev tool).

title: getReader()-throws finding misses the null-stream guard 67 lines above
detail: Review flagged lib/subprocess.ts:210 'getReader() throws outside try/catch, leaves job stuck running'. But a guard at lines 143-152 checks `if (!proc.stdout || !proc.stderr)` and finalizes-as-failed BEFORE the getReader calls are reached. The review lane pattern-matched the call site without scanning upward for an existing guard. Verified 2026-06-19: guard present, finding is dead. Frontend useJobs.ts:16 left unchanged — its job_start listener is now live. bun test 546 pass. title: lib/knowledge-extractor.ts parseCaptionField reads legacy flat key .caption but run.py's caption writer ALWAYS wraps in styles.<style>.caption — all modern T2I records silently excluded from DeepSeek learning + infinite re-captioning
detail: CONFIRMED high-severity correctness bug (2026-06-21T02:18, confidence 95, BOTH verified findings were this bug at two sites). lib/knowledge-extractor.ts scanOutputDirs() calls parseCaptionField(captionRaw.caption) (line ~84) and generateMissingCaptions() re-reads the same way (line ~193), but run.py's caption writer ALWAYS wraps output in a `styles` map: python/mlx-movie-director/app/commands/caption.py `_normalize_caption_file` (line ~342-358) re-wraps even legacy flat files into `styles.<style>.caption`, and `_load_existing_styles` reads from `styles`. The on-disk shape is {styles:{review:{caption:'{overall:...}'}}}. So captionRaw.caption is `undefined` for every file written by run.py, parseCaptionField(undefined) returns null, and every T2I record is forced to hasCaption=false / qualityScore=null. TWO compounding effects: (1) silently excludes ALL current-generation T2I records from DeepSeek learning (the knowledge pipeline never ingests any modern output); (2) the post-caption re-read path (line ~193) means freshly-generated review captions are immediately discarded — rec.hasCaption stays false and the record is re-queued for captioning FOREVER (the 'Captions' tab missing-count never decreases). This is a confirmed KB-flagged LEVER (2026-06-20T23-13 reader/writer asymmetry), now materialized to exact lines. Note normalizeCaptionFile (captionFormat.ts) and the gallery API already handle the multi-style shape correctly — only the knowledge extractor was left on the legacy path. FIX: replace both parseCaptionField(captionRaw.caption) sites with normalize + pickCaptionStyle (same helper the gallery API uses). This is the SECOND distinct high-severity open defect in lib/knowledge-extractor.ts (the first is the callDeepSeek AbortSignal-timeout, pattern-high-triage-candidates-2026-06-19) — making lib/knowledge-extractor.ts the #1 triage target. A targeted files:[lib/knowledge-extractor.ts] effort:medium+fix:true run on a clean tree should clear both.

title: Extract duplicated cross-origin allowlist into a shared lib/origin.ts helper (adopted 2026-06-21T03:52) — closes the security-fix-not-ported-to-sibling drift
detail: ADOPTED fix (2026-06-21T03:52, effort:low+fix:true, one of the 5 applied): the Origin/Host defense (extract port from Host header with /:(\d+)$/, default '3099', build allowedOrigins=[127.0.0.1,localhost,[::1]]:${port}, reject if !includes(origin)) was copy-pasted in full in BOTH api/routes.ts (lines ~96-117) and api/ws.ts (lines ~23-40). A security fix applied to one site is easy to miss in the other (the cross-origin-allowlist-duplication KB failure mode). Extracted a single originAllowed(origin, host) (plus DEFAULT_PORT constant) into a shared lib/origin.ts module; both sites now import + call it. The two prior distinct 403 response bodies ('Invalid request' when host absent vs 'Cross-origin request blocked' otherwise) are preserved by checking !host AFTER originAllowed returns false. Generalizes: when the same security/defense logic appears in two api/* entry points (HTTP + WS are the two in this server), extract a shared helper into lib/ so a fix can never drift between them. This was surfaced as a verified finding on a clean-tree full-scope fix:true run and applied with 0 regressions — a model for how the low-effort fix path delivers substantive (not cosmetic) refactors.

title: Replace long sequential if/else API dispatch chains with a declarative STATIC_ROUTES + PREFIX_ROUTES table loop — adopted 2026-06-21T03:52
detail: ADOPTED refactor pattern (2026-06-21T03:52, effort:low+fix:true, one of the 5 applied): api/routes.ts handleApi had a ~30-check sequential if/else dispatch chain (one branch per route). Replaced with a declarative route table built at module scope: a STATIC_ROUTES array of {method, pathname, handler} for exact matches and a PREFIX_ROUTES array of {method, prefix, handler} for dynamic-id matches (currently /api/jobs/ GET and DELETE). handleApi now loops STATIC_ROUTES first (exact match), then PREFIX_ROUTES. LOAD-BEARING detail: static-first matching preserves the original ordering where /api/jobs/last (GET) and /api/jobs/all (DELETE) must win over the /api/jobs/ prefix routes, so those paths are never mis-read as job ids — documented inline. The CSRF/origin guard stays at the top of handleApi unchanged; all handler signatures and response shapes are byte-for-byte equivalent. Generalizes to any Bun/Bun.serve API module where a long method+pathname if/else has grown past ~15 branches: a route table is more maintainable, makes ordering explicit, and surfaces dead/duplicate routes. Applied with 0 regressions on a clean-tree fix:true run.
